antibiotics, particularly macromolecules and quinolone, are widely spread in the environment and are mainly derived from STPs, and that the most abundant compounds are clarithromycin, spiramycin, ciprofloxaxin and ofloxaxin.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence of antibiotics in the environment, and their fate in sewage treatment plants ( STPs).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

antibiotics are widespread environmental contaminants and that STPs are confirmed major sources of the contamination, and this is a matter of concern because of the possible risks for the ecosystem, for the environment and for the health of humans and animals.
antibiotics in the environment are not a negligible problem and should be taken in consideration in environmental and health risk assessment.
antibiotics are a new group of emerging pollutants, which are present at low concentrations, but are still able to affect the ecosystem and human beings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the environmental loads of macrolides and fluoroquinolones are comparable to those of other emerging pollutants, such as the endocrine disruptors, which are currently under intense investigation and are subject to stringent regulations in many countries.
the antibiotics are not removed in STP and are still present in the treated effluents.
the Italian aquatic environment is heavily contaminated with a wide range of antibiotic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environmental loads of antibiotics are not decreasing in Italy, and that the environmental fate of antibiotics in aquatic systems is still not well understood.
the Italian STPs are a significant source of antibiotics to the aquatic environment, which should be considered for the development of more efficient treatment processes.
, in order to protect the ecosystem and human population, it is necessary to reduce the use of these compounds and, at the same time, improve the efficiency of wastewater treatments.
